claims.text: The investigated alloy has composition Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Slow cooling after arc melting produces a complex microstructure containing multiple crystalline phases.
The phases formed during slow cooling are primary non-eutectic phases.
Very rapid cooling by melt spinning can produce an amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 structure.
The rapidly quenched amorphous alloy is vulnerable to crystallization during reheating.
Phosphorus modifies the alloy's thermal behavior and promotes amorphization or enhanced glass-forming ability during rapid cooling.
The proposed intervention is a 1–2 second isothermal hold near 0.9·Tg following or interrupting an ultra-rapid quench.
The intervention applies at quench rates of approximately 10^5–10^6 K/s.
A brief hold near 0.9·Tg will enhance short-range atomic ordering and structural relaxation in the amorphous matrix.
Structural relaxation during the hold will reduce internal stresses.
The hold-induced relaxed state will reduce atomic mobility.
Enhanced short-range order and relaxation will minimize the driving force for nucleation of primary crystalline phases.
The proposed lock-in effect will decrease crystallization during subsequent cooling and reheating.
Held samples will retain a higher amorphous fraction than otherwise identical samples quenched without the hold.
Held samples will exhibit delayed or reduced DSC crystallization exotherms during reheating.
The proposed effect is expected during reheating at approximately 20 K/min.
Ultra-rapid quenching at 10^5–10^6 K/s without a hold produces an amorphous state that crystallizes readily upon reheating.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant increase in amorphous retention or a delay or reduction of crystallization exotherms relative to the no-hold control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hold is described as occurring immediately after ultra-rapid quenching, but also as pausing the quench before continued cooling. These imply different thermal histories: a completed quench followed by reheating to 0.9·Tg versus an interrupted quench held at 0.9·Tg.
